# RedHanded

Makes new code prove itself before an agent trusts it. Runs npm packages and agent skills on a disposable machine baited with fake credentials and a fake internet, and reports what they tried to do. Fixed rules decide the verdict. Text under test cannot change it.

Verdicts: CLEAN (allow), REVIEW (ask a human), HIGH and CRITICAL (block).

## MCP

POST /mcp, stateless HTTP. Tools: check_package, check_lockfile_change, compare_versions, find_safe_version, check_skill, get_scan_report.

## HTTP

POST /api/scan {"package": "name@version"} returns {"job": id}
POST /api/scan {"tarball": "<base64 npm tarball, up to 2 MB>"} returns {"job": id}; real malware is welcome
POST /api/lockfile {"new_lockfile": "...", "old_lockfile": "..."} returns {"job": id}
POST /api/compare {"name": "package", "version": "1.2.3"} returns {"job": id}; the result lists what is new since the version before
POST /api/repair {"name": "package", "version": "1.2.3"} returns {"job": id}; the result names the closest version the rules cleared
POST /api/skill {"skill_md": "..."} or {"files": {"SKILL.md": "...", "scripts/x.sh": "..."}} returns {"job": id}
GET /api/jobs/{id} returns state, verdict and result
GET /api/scans/{scan_id} returns the report and evidence

Limit: 12 runs an hour per address.

A model reads whatever ran clean and can raise it to REVIEW, never clear or block it. On 898 real malicious packages it took CLEAN from 369 to 104, and asked a person about 2 of 441 unseen packages.

A verdict that lets code through expires after 24 hours and the bytes run again. A block never expires.

Containment was measured, not assumed: while the 100 most network-active malware samples ran, 250 outside hosts were tried and 0 appeared on the real network card, with positive controls. A Claude Code hook (hooks/redhanded_guard.py) refuses a blocked install and names the version that proved clean.
